nodes.name: Lemma 4.1
Lemma C.2
nodes.statement:
Consider the Adam algorithm in Algorithm Adam and suppose that Assumption 2.1 - 2.3 hold. Then for any initial point, and $T \geq 1$, the following results hold
\begin{align*}
&\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,T}(f(w_{T})-f^*)]=\mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\|\eta_{v_{t}}\circ g_{t}\|^{2}\right)+\mathcal{O}(1),  
\\&\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\left[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\zeta_{i}(t)\right]=\mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\|\eta_{v_{t}}\circ g_{t}\|^{2}\right)+\mathcal{O}(1),
\\&\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\mathbb{E}\left[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Delta_{t,i}|\nabla_{i} f(u_{t})m_{t-1,i}|\right]=\mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\|\eta_{v_{t}}\circ g_{t}\|^{2}\right)+\mathcal{O}(1).
\end{align*}
The specific form of the constants hidden behind the \(\mathcal{O}()\) notation can be found in Equation (55) and Equation (56). All constants depend on the initial point and the constants in our required assumptions (excluding $1/\mu$).

nodes.name: Lemma C.3
Lemma C.4
Lemma C.5
Lemma C.7
Lemma C.8
nodes.statement:
Consider the Adam algorithm defined in Algorithm Adam and suppose that Assumption 2.1 - 2.3 hold. Then for any initial point, for all $T\ge 1,\ i\in[1,d],$ there is
\[\mathbb{E}({S^{3/4}_{T}})=\begin{cases} 
\mathcal{O}({T^{3/4}}), & \text{if } \delta \in (0,1], \\
\mathcal{O}({T^{3/4}}\ln^{3/2} T), & \text{if } \delta = 0,
\end{cases}\]
where constants hidden in $\mathcal{O}()$ depend on the initial point and the constants in our required assumptions (excluding $1/\mu$).

nodes.name: Lemma C.10
Lemma C.9
nodes.statement:
Under Assumptions 2.1 - 2.3, consider the Adam algorithm (Algorithm Adam) with the hyperparameters specified in Subsection 2.4. Then, for any $t \geq 1$, the following inequality holds
\[
\sup_{t \geq 1} \mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t} \Sigma_{v_{t}}] <\begin{cases} 
\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,2}\Sigma_{v_{1}}]+(A+2L_{f}B)M_{\delta}+C, & \text{if } \delta \in (0,1], \\
\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,2}\Sigma_{v_{1}}]+(A+2L_{f}B)M_{0}\ln^{2}t+C, & \text{if } \delta = 0.
\end{cases}
\]
Furthermore, if $\lambda > 1$, then 
\[\sup_{t \geq 1} \mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Sigma_{v_{t}}] < \begin{cases} 
\big((A+2L_{f}B)M_{\delta}+C\big)\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\frac{1}{(t+1)^{\lambda}}, & \text{if } \delta \in (0,1] \\
\big((A+2L_{f}B)M_{0}+C\big)\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\frac{\ln^{2}t}{(t+1)^{\lambda}}, & \text{if } \delta = 0
\end{cases}<+\infty.\] Additionally,
\[\sup_{t \geq 1}\Sigma_{v_{t}} < +\infty \quad \text{a.s.}\]

nodes.name: Lemma B.3
Lemma C.1
nodes.statement:
For $\Pi_{\Delta,T}$ defined in Equation (7), for any $T \geq 0$ and any $p \geq 1$, the $p$-th moment of its reciprocal is bounded, i.e.,
\[\mathbb{E}\left[\Pi^{-p}_{\Delta,T}\right] < C_{v,d,p} < +\infty,\]
where $C_{v,d,p}$ is a constant that depends only on $v$, $d$, and $p$.

Moreover, we have that $\Pi^{-1}_{\Delta,\infty} := \lim_{t \rightarrow +\infty} \Pi^{-1}_{\Delta,t} < +\infty \ \ \text{a.s.}$, and for any $p \geq 1$, the $p$-th moment of $\Pi^{-1}_{\Delta,\infty}$ exists, with
\[\mathbb{E}\left[\Pi^{-p}_{\Delta,\infty}\right] \leq C_{v,d,p} < +\infty.\]

nodes.name: Theorem 3.1
Theorem 3.2
nodes.statement:
Under Assumptions 2.1--2.3, consider the Adam with hyperparameters specified in Subsection 2.4 with \( \gamma > 1 \) and \( \delta > 0 \). Then, the gradients of the Adam converge to zero almost surely, i.e.,
\(
\lim_{t \to \infty} \|\nabla f(w_t)\| = 0 \quad \text{a.s.}
\)

nodes.name: Theorem 3.3
nodes.statement:
Under Assumptions 2.1--2.3, consider the Adam with hyperparameters specified in Subsection 2.4 with \( \gamma > 1 \) and \( \delta > 0 \). Then, the gradients of the Adam converge to zero in the \( L_{1} \) sense, i.e.,
\(
\lim_{t \to \infty}\mathbb{E}[\|\nabla f(w_t)\|] = 0.
\)

nodes.name: Lemma C.6
nodes.statement:
Under Assumptions 2.1 - 2.3, consider the Adam algorithm (Algorithm Adam) with hyperparameters as specified in Subsection 2.4, where \( \delta > 0 \). Then, there exists a subsequence \( \{w_{c_{t}}\}_{t \geq 1} \) such that its gradients converge to zero almost surely, i.e.,
\(
\lim_{t \to \infty} \|\nabla f(w_{c_t})\| = 0 \quad \text{a.s.}
\)
